title: Zigzag Conversion

understand.question: If you write a string's characters down and diagonally up across numRows horizontal rows in a zigzag wave, what string do you get when reading row by row from top to bottom?
understand.plainExplanation: Imagine writing letters onto lined notebook paper with numRows lines: go straight down from line 0 to the bottom line, bounce diagonally back up to line 0, and repeat. Then read line 0 from left to right, followed by line 1, and so on.
understand.inputMeaning: A string s and a positive integer numRows (>= 1).
understand.outputMeaning: The concatenated string formed by reading each row left-to-right from row 0 down to row numRows - 1.
rules: If numRows == 1 or numRows >= s.length, there is no zigzag bounce — return s unchanged.
Do NOT emit spaces between diagonal letters; each row simply collects its characters in order.
Direction flips only when reaching row 0 (start moving down) or row numRows - 1 (start moving up).

terms.definition: A string buffer dedicated to one horizontal line (0 .. numRows - 1) that collects letters in the exact order they land on that row.
The number of characters in one full down-and-up wave: 2 * (numRows - 1) when numRows > 1.

example1.whyValid: Writing "INFINITY" across 3 rows places indices 0:'I'->r0, 1:'N'->r1, 2:'F'->r2, 3:'I'->r1, 4:'N'->r0, 5:'I'->r1, 6:'T'->r2, 7:'Y'->r1. Reading row 0 ("IN"), row 1 ("NIIY"), and row 2 ("FT") yields "INNIIYFT".

diagram.caption: Row 0: IN, Row 1: NIIY, Row 2: FT -> "INNIIYFT".

example2.whyEdgeCase: When numRows == 1, cycle length 2 * (numRows - 1) is 0! Any formula dividing or stepping by cycle length would loop infinitely unless numRows == 1 returns s early.

steps.title: Move down column 0: I -> row 0, N -> row 1, F -> row 2
steps.description: Start at row = 0 with dir = -1. At row 0, dir flips to +1; append 'I' (row 0), 'N' (row 1), 'F' (row 2). Reaching bottom row 2 prepares dir to flip to -1.

steps.title: Bounce diagonally up: I -> row 1, N -> row 0
steps.description: dir flipped to -1 at row 2. Step upward placing 'I' onto row 1 and 'N' onto row 0. Hitting top row 0 flips dir back to +1.

state.caption: Upward diagonal complete; direction flips back down.

steps.title: Finish remaining letters 'I', 'T', 'Y' and join rows
steps.description: Append 'I' (row 1), 'T' (row 2), and bounce up to 'Y' (row 1). Concatenate row 0 + row 1 + row 2 -> "IN" + "NIIY" + "FT" = "INNIIYFT".

approaches.name: Row-by-Row Simulation with Direction Flag
approaches.recommendedTradeOff: Visits each character once in O(n) time without needing 2D blank cells or tricky index arithmetic.
approaches.coreIdeaSummary: Keep one buffer per row and bounce a row cursor between 0 and numRows - 1.
approaches.coreIdea: Maintain an array of numRows string builders. Append each character to rows[curRow], flipping direction at row 0 and row numRows - 1.
steps: If numRows == 1 or numRows >= len(s), return s.
Create numRows empty row buffers and set row = 0, dir = -1.
For each char ch: if row == 0 or row == numRows - 1, negate dir; append ch to rows[row]; set row += dir.
Join all row buffers and return.
approaches.whyItWorks: Negating dir at both endpoints makes row oscillate cleanly: 0, 1, ..., numRows-1, numRows-2, ..., 0.

approaches.name: Direct Cycle Index Jumping
approaches.coreIdeaSummary: Visit characters directly in output row order using cycle = 2 * (numRows - 1).
approaches.coreIdea: Each row repeats every cycle = 2 * (numRows - 1) indices. Interior rows (0 < r < numRows - 1) have one extra diagonal index at j + cycle - 2 * r.
steps: For row r from 0 to numRows - 1, step j = r, r + cycle, ...: append s[j], and if 0 < r < numRows - 1 and j + cycle - 2*r < n, also append s[j + cycle - 2*r].
approaches.whyItWorks: Inside each cycle of length 2*(numRows - 1), the vertical column puts row r at offset r and the upward diagonal puts row r at offset cycle - r.
approaches.whenToUse: When you want zero intermediate row buffers (only output storage).
approaches.diagramNote: Cycle length is 2*(3-1) = 4. Row 1 reads vertical indices (1, 5) interleaved with diagonal indices (3, 7).

diagram.caption: Reads row 1 directly via cycle step 4: indices 1, 3, 5, 7.
